item.title: Issues Uploading New Assets
item.content:encoded:
Resolved —

All issues affecting uploads to DatoCMS using Cloudflare R2 in the EU region have now been fully resolved.

Uploads are operating normally again across the default EU R2 storage as well as custom storage configurations. We are no longer seeing errors related to this incident.

Monitoring —

The issue affecting uploads to DatoCMS using Cloudflare R2 in the EU region appears to be resolved at this time.

Uploads are currently working as expected, including on the default Cloudflare R2 (EU) storage. We are continuing to monitor the situation closely to ensure stability.

Investigating —

We’re currently investigating an issue affecting the ability to upload new assets to DatoCMS. The issue impacts Cloudflare R2 buckets in the EU jurisdiction, which is the default storage configuration.

Uploads to custom storage solutions are working as expected, indicating the problem is specific to Cloudflare R2 in the EU region.

Our team is actively investigating the root cause and working with the relevant providers to restore full functionality as quickly as possible. We will share further updates as soon as we have more information.

item.title: Incident Report - API Outage on December 2, 2025
item.content:encoded:
Resolved —

On December 2 at 13:13 CET, our API was unavailable for 9 minutes during a deployment, causing errors when accessing the CMS interface.

What happened

During a routine database migration deployment, code that depended on a not-yet-created database table was accidentally included. This caused the API to fail until we identified and rolled back the changes.

Prevention

We're implementing stricter code review checks to ensure migration-only deployments don't include dependent code, and adding automated tests to catch this type of issue before deployment.

We apologise for the disruption and appreciate your patience.

  • DatoCMS APIs (CDA and CMA)
  • datocms-assets.com
  • The dashboard and admin area

Our systems remain fully operational, and we are actively monitoring the situation while Cloudflare works to resolve the upstream problem. We will provide updates as soon as more information becomes available.

item.title: [Retrospective] Gatsby project build failures caused by missing records in GraphQL responses
item.content:encoded:
Resolved —

On August 4th, 2025, starting from 14:00 UTC, some customers reported issues building their Gatsby projects that use our gatsby-source-datocms plugin due to records being missing from their GraphQL responses, despite being present in the CMS admin area.

The issue was related to a recent change in our code that caused pagination issues with the records fetched by our gatsby-source-datocms plugin. This prevented some records from being visible in the Gatsby GraphQL responses.

A rollback of that change was deployed on August 5th at 7:15 UTC.

A regression test has been added to ensure that this particular issue with pagination won't happen again.

item.title: 2025-07-15: Performance degradation
item.content:encoded:
Resolved —

The developers traced the issue to an auto-scaling issue in a part of our infrastructure, where a cluster wasn't properly adding more resources as quickly as needed in order to keep up performance under load. We've since tweaked the scaling configuration and it should not happen again. Our apologies for the slowdown!

Resolved —

Several customers reported intermittent API performance degradation starting from about 1530 UTC (1730 CEST, 8:30am PST) lasting about an hour. Performance appears to be restored now, but we will continue to monitor the situation and investigate the underlying cause. Please email support@datocms.com if you are still experiencing any performance issues.

item.title: Response Time Degradation
item.content:encoded:
Resolved —

Postmortem: we made some changes in our Cloudflare configuration to enable a higher cache hit ratio. We relied on the fact that Cloudflare explicitly states that they support URLs up to 16KB long:
https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/#request-limits
Turns out it's not true: we asked for more info from Cloudflare; in the meantime, we reverted our optimization.

Monitoring —

Our services experienced increased response times for 12 minutes between 4:25 CEST and 4:37 CEST today. The issue was promptly identified and resolved by our engineering team. Please note that the status page graphs incorrectly show a +50-minute degradation period due to a misconfiguration in our reporting system. This does not reflect the actual duration of the incident. The reporting system has been corrected. All services are now operating normally with regular response times.

item.title: PDFs rendering as thumbnail images on Chrome & Edge
item.content:encoded:
Resolved —

The issue has been resolved.

Investigating —

PDFs served from datocms-assets.com are currently showing up as image thumbnails rather than PDF files for Chromium-based browsers (Chrome and Edge). Firefox and Safari are not affected.

A current workaround is to append ?skip-default-optimizations to the end of the URL, like: https://www.datocms-assets.com/123456/123456789-your-file.pdf?skip-default-optimizations

That should allow the PDF to load normally.

We are working on a permanent resolution and will update here as soon as we can.

item.title: Cloudflare: Cloudflare Pages, Workers KV and Cloudflare Access Availability Issues
item.content:encoded:
Resolved —

We have further analyzed what happened in this incident and here's a longer explanation.

We use Cloudflare workers at the edge of our platform to cache GraphQL requests and block traffic that goes over hard limits, for example for people with cancelled subscriptions. To block these projects we save the information in the Cloudflare KV.

When Cloudflare KV was down our workers were breaking causing the cache to be bypassed.

So all the GraphQL requests were going straight to our servers causing an unusual load that slowed down everything very significantly. Only a minority of requests timed out, but still the user experience was significantly affected and everything seemed down. Furthermore, because everything hit our servers the rate-limits for GraphQL requests were hit much more frequently.

To avoid this from happening in the future we are going to improve our workers to avoid them for breaking in case of the KV service being down. If this has to happen again at least the caching will keep working. We didn't anticipate that the workers and KV storage might break independently, but we'll improve this part of the infrastructure soon.

Resolved —

This incident is now resolved. The impact start time was 2023-10-30, 20:03 UTC, and the end time was 2023-10-30, 20:35 UTC.

The incident caused response times to be longer than usual on CDA API. We will investigate the issue, and we'll get back here with more details.

item.title: Rollbar security notice
item.content:encoded:
Resolved —

On September 8th Rollbar announced a security incident.

Rollbar is our error monitoring tool, where we send stacktraces of errors collected on frontend and backend systems.

All the details of the incident here: https://rollbar.com/compliance/nob_sep7th/

In brief, our Rollbar access tokens might have been accessed by a third party, but Rollbar has no evidence of this happening. This means that our traces could have been read by someone else. In our implementation, before sending the traces to Rollbar we strip any personal information that might be present or any access token to DatoCMS projects.

Apart from the posted data in the traces nothing else could have been exposed to third parties.

In any case, on Sep 12th we have rotated all our tokens and deleted all the stack traces that were present in Rollbar. To this day we don't have any evidence that any of our data was accessed by a malicious third party.

item.title: CMS interface unreachable
item.content:encoded:
Resolved —

CMS interface has been unavailable for around 6 hours from around 12AM to 6AM UTC on the 29th of September.

All APIs were up and running, meaning that all the sites that were using our APIs were unaffected.

We have identified the root cause of the issue in a our Nginx + auto SSL configuration. We use auto SSL (a Lua plugin for Nginx) to issue certificates for new custom CMS addresses (like datocms.yourdomain.com). At the beginning of the issue a new site has been created with a custom domain that wasn't properly configured. This caused auto SSL to fail and try different connections using IPv6, which wasn't configured on the server. This caused Nginx to stop responding even if the service was up. So on server restart everything worked as expected.

We have now added an IPv6 address to the machine to prevent this from happening again.

Also our status page is showing the downtime of the issue and we are putting in place systems to handle these type of events in a quicker manner.

Monitoring —

Imgix has rolled out a fix and is monitoring the situation which should be back to normal for most users: https://status.imgix.com/incidents/bg0msyrz9f17

Identified —

Imgix is our service provider for asset caching and manipulation. They are seeing errors that are affecting our asset uploads and serving. Read all the details on their status page: https://status.imgix.com/incidents/bg0msyrz9f17

item.title: Database maintenance
item.content:encoded:
Completed —

All the systems are back online, sorry for the inconvenience. Enjoy your new Media Area! :)

Scheduled —

We are going to perform a maintenance task on our master database and we expect all our APIs to be unavailable for around 15 minutes.

This task is going to be necessary to prepare for the upcoming changes in the media area.

item.title: Increased number of timeouts
item.content:encoded:
Resolved —

We have identified and improved the query that has caused a snowball error in our database bringing most of the queries to timeouts.

The total number of record versions saved in our DB is growing fast and it's causing new challenges for us. We'll monitor the situation in the next few days. Hopefully we'll be faster next time as we have also improved our error reporting from the DB.

Identified —

We have found the root cause in a slow query that was bringing down the database for everyone.

We have limited the query duration and the status seems back to normal.

We are monitoring and trying to release a stable fix.

Investigating —

We are seeing an increased number of calls timing out.

When we see a spike of timeouts we can see errors across different endpoints.

We are investigating the root cause of the issue and we'll report back as soon as possible.

item.title: Network connection issues
item.content:encoded:
Resolved —

Two outages happened together on 24th of June 2019 impacting different areas of DatoCMS.

One was Cloudflare: https://www.cloudflarestatus.com/incidents/46z55mdhg0t5 which would have impacted the GraphQL endpoint which had given time outs to certain IP ranges.

The other was with Heroku, which have impacted both GraphQL and REST APIs: https://status.heroku.com/incidents/1804

If you want more information or leave a comment, you can do that here: https://community.datocms.com/t/downtime-june-24th-2019/53

item.title: Imgix Degraded Performance
item.content:encoded:
Resolved —

The issue is now resolved.

Investigating —

Imgix is currently having some troubles returning images in some particular regions, we're investigating. For more information: https://status.imgix.com/

item.title: Big upgrade of React codebase
item.content:encoded:
Completed —

We made it! We received a bunch of reports of weird things happening in some edge-cases, but overall it was a pretty smooth migration. Thanks for your help!

Scheduled —

We're going to deploy some big internal code refactorings to the React app that powers the DatoCMS administrative areas. We'll follow the deploy closely, but if you happen to find any kind of annoyance/bug, please contact us via support@datocms.com or chat.

item.title: Routing errors
item.content:encoded:
Resolved —

This issue is now resolved.

Monitoring —

Heroku has pushed a fix and we are seeing error rates decrease. We will continue monitoring to ensure that this issue is fully resolved.

Investigating —

We are investigating an issue on our provider (Heroku) that is causing instability in managing applications. You may experience routing errors contacting both our CDA ad CMA.

item.title: Request Timeout
item.content:encoded:
Resolved —

This issue is now resolved.

Monitoring —

The problem seems to have disappeared, we're monitoring the situation.

Investigating —

You may experience some errors contacting both our CDA ad CMA, a lot of request are failing due to timeout. Investingating.

item.title: Scheduled Database Maintenance
item.content:encoded:
Completed —

Maintenance was successfully completed!

Scheduled —

We're performing database maintenance at this time. During the maintenance window, parts DatoCMS may be sporadically unavailable for a small percentage of customers.

item.title: Low Level Of 5xx Errors From Content Management API
item.content:encoded:
Resolved —

The problem is now resolved

Monitoring —

We identified the source of the problem and shipped a fix. We'll continue monitoring the situation

Investigating —

We are seeing a low level of 5xx errors for some Delivery API traffic, we are investigating the issue.

item.title: High Level Of 5xx Errors From Content Management API
item.content:encoded:
Resolved —

This incident has been resolved, we'll keep monitoring the situation.

Investigating —

We are seeing an high level of 5xx errors on the Content Management API traffic for some projects, we are investigating the issue.

item.title: CDN Maintenance
item.content:encoded:
Completed —

All systems are back to normal.

Scheduled —

Tomorrow, Friday 21st from 9:00 CET to 10:00 CET we’ll deploy some important infrastructure enhancements to the GraphQL Content Delivery API that should significantly lower latency and response times. The CDA will keep on work during the upgrade, but might respond slower. We’ll keep you updated during the process.

item.title: Slow Responses And Intermittent 503 Error Codes
item.content:encoded:
Resolved —

The problem was due to some memory corruption issues on the server caused by some C extensions. We tracked down the issue and shipped a fix. We’ll continue monitoring the situation.

Investigating —

We’re receiving feedback of slow responses and intermittent 503 error codes on our Content Management API, we’ve doubled up our server resources and investigating in the meantime

item.title: Database Maintenance
item.content:encoded:
Completed —

All systems are back to normal

Scheduled —

The actual maintenance impact should be contained to 15 minutes.

We’ll be upgrading the software running our databases. During this period of time the Content Management API and Content Delivery API will be completely unavailable.

item.title: Master Database Maintenance
item.content:encoded:
Completed —

All systems are back to normal

Scheduled —

We will perform some maintenance over our master database and will need to bring down the site for a few short minutes while we do the switch. Total downtime is not expected to exceed 5 minutes.

item.title: Unscheduled Maintenance
item.content:encoded:
Completed —

All systems are back to normal.

Scheduled —

We are performing maintenance to update how DatoCMS handles paymentes and invocing. No impact is expected to production services throughout the maintenance. An update will be posted once the maintenance is complete.

item.title: Low Level Of 5xx Errors From Content Management API
item.content:encoded:
Resolved —

This incident has been resolved.

Investigating —

We are seeing a low level of 5xx errors for some Delivery API traffic, we are investigating the issue.

item.title: Administrative Areas Unreachable
item.content:encoded:
Resolved —

Digital Ocean has just implemented a fix. More details here: https://status.digitalocean.com/incidents/fq8nt7bfrclx

We’ll switch back to our original instance once everything is resolved.

Monitoring —

The duplicate of the machine is online. Everything should be working, but we’re double checking everything.

Identified —

The duplicate of the machine is almost ready, we should be up and running in approx 15 minutes.

Identified —

The machine is reachable and responds to ping if we perform the request from other locations, so this seems like a localized issue. We’re currently working on duplicating the machine.

Identified —

We’ve identified the issue. The Digital Ocean machine that hosts is having some networking/routing issues: we’ll keep you posted in real-time.

Investigating —

The server that hosts our administrative area interface is down.
